title: Hosea Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hosea chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hosea Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hosea Chapter 13.

questions.question: What happened to Ephraim when he offended in Baal?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:1 states that when Ephraim offended in Baal, he died.

questions.question: According to Hosea 13, what have the people made from their silver?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:2 says they have made molten images of their silver.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 13 describes the idols as the work of the craftsmen.
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:2 explicitly says the idols are all the work of the craftsmen.

questions.question: What metaphor is used in Hosea 13 to describe what Ephraim shall be like?
options: The morning cloud and early dew
questions.correctAnswer: The morning cloud and early dew
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:3 compares Ephraim to the morning cloud and early dew that passeth away.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 13 says there is no saviour besides the LORD.
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:4 states there is no saviour beside the LORD.

questions.question: Where did the LORD say He knew Israel?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:5 says the LORD knew Israel in the wilderness.

questions.question: True or False: According to Hosea 13, Israel's heart was humble and they remembered God.
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:6 explains that their heart was exalted and they forgot God.

questions.question: What did Israel do according to Hosea 13:6 after being filled according to their pasture?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:6 states they were filled, their heart was exalted, and therefore they forgot God.

questions.question: What do the people say about the calves in Hosea 13?
options: Let the men that sacrifice kiss the calves
The calves are sacred and untouchable
We will offer calves as a sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: Let the men that sacrifice kiss the calves
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:2 records the phrase, 'Let the men that sacrifice kiss the calves.'

questions.question: In Hosea 13, what will happen to Ephraim according to the metaphor in verse 3?
options: They will grow strong like a tree
They will be as the morning cloud and early dew that pass away
They will be blessed with abundance
questions.correctAnswer: They will be as the morning cloud and early dew that pass away
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:3 uses this metaphor to describe Ephraim's fleeting nature.

questions.question: Who is the LORD referring to when He says, 'I did know thee in the wilderness'?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:5 states that the LORD knew Israel in the wilderness.

questions.question: True or False: Ephraim spoke confidently and was humble according to Hosea 13:1.
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:1 says Ephraim spake trembling but exalted himself, not that he was humble.

questions.question: According to Hosea 13:4, where is the LORD thy God from?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:4 states, 'I am the LORD thy God from the land of Egypt.'

questions.question: What do the people make idols according to, as stated in Hosea 13?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:2 says the idols were made according to their own understanding.

questions.question: In Hosea 13, what is the reason given for Israel forgetting God?
options: Their heart was exalted because they were filled
questions.correctAnswer: Their heart was exalted because they were filled
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:6 explains that according to their pasture they were filled, their heart was exalted, therefore they forgot God.

medium.title: Hosea Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hosea Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Hosea 13:7, how does God say He will act toward Israel due to their sins?
options: As a lion and a leopard observing them
As a shepherd guiding them gently
As a father teaching his son
questions.correctAnswer: As a lion and a leopard observing them
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:7 states that God will be unto them as a lion and as a leopard by the way will He observe them, indicating a fierce and watchful judgment because of their sins. This connects with verse 8 where God further describes His judgment as a bear and lion.

questions.question: What imagery does Hosea 13:8 use to describe God's judgment on Israel?
options: A bear bereaved of her whelps and a lion devouring them
A gentle rain nourishing the earth
A mighty fortress protecting the weak
A shepherd leading his sheep to safety
questions.correctAnswer: A bear bereaved of her whelps and a lion devouring them
questions.explanation: Verse 8 uses the imagery of a bereaved bear and a lion to describe God's fierce and consuming judgment on Israel, emphasizing the severity of their punishment as a consequence of their rebellion.

questions.question: What hope does Hosea 13:9 offer to Israel despite their self-destruction?
options: In their kings lies their salvation
In their idols lies their refuge
In their warriors lies their strength
questions.explanation: Though Israel has destroyed themselves, Hosea 13:9 declares that help is found in God alone, highlighting the theme of reliance on God despite failures.

questions.question: According to Hosea 13:10, what role does God claim to fulfill for Israel, and what question does He pose?
options: He will be their king and asks who else can save them in their cities
He will be their judge and asks who else can condemn them
He will be their prophet and asks who else can teach them
He will be their shepherd and asks who else can lead them
questions.correctAnswer: He will be their king and asks who else can save them in their cities
questions.explanation: Verse 10 states God will be Israel's king and questions the existence of any other savior in their cities, emphasizing God's sovereign role as their ultimate ruler and deliverer.

questions.question: What does Hosea 13:11 reveal about God's response to Israel's request for a king?
options: God gave a king in anger and took him away in wrath
God blessed the king and extended his reign forever
God ignored their request and sent prophets instead
God gave a king to bring peace and prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: God gave a king in anger and took him away in wrath
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:11 explains that the king was given by God in anger and removed in wrath, showing God's displeasure with Israel's demand and the consequences of their rebellion.

questions.question: What does Hosea 13:12 say about Ephraim's sin?
options: His iniquity is bound up and his sin is hidden
His sin is openly confessed and forgiven
He has no sin to repent of
questions.correctAnswer: His iniquity is bound up and his sin is hidden
questions.explanation: Verse 12 states that Ephraim's iniquity is bound up and his sin is hid, indicating that the sin is deeply entrenched and not openly repented of, which contributes to Israel's judgment.

questions.question: How does Hosea 13:9 and 13:10 together teach about trust and leadership?
options: Despite self-destruction, trust is in God as king, not in human judges or kings
Trust should be placed in earthly kings and judges for salvation
Self-destruction is final with no help available
Leaders are irrelevant to Israel's salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Despite self-destruction, trust is in God as king, not in human judges or kings
questions.explanation: Verse 9 acknowledges Israel's self-destruction but points to God as help, while verse 10 emphasizes God as king and questions the efficacy of human judges and requested kings, highlighting reliance on God over human leadership.

questions.question: What lesson about humility and repentance can we learn from Hosea 13:12 in the context of hidden sin?
options: Unacknowledged sin leads to judgment and hinders repentance
Hidden sin is easily forgiven without confession
Pride is acceptable if sin is hidden
Sin does not affect our standing with God if it's secret
questions.correctAnswer: Unacknowledged sin leads to judgment and hinders repentance
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:12 teaches that Ephraim's sin is bound and hidden, implying a lack of acknowledgment that prevents true repentance and subjects them to further judgment, stressing the need for humility and confession.

questions.question: A believer struggles with trusting human leaders for deliverance. How does Hosea 13:10-11 guide this believer's understanding?
options: God is the true king and deliverer, and human kings may fail or be given in anger
Human kings are the ultimate source of salvation
Judges and princes are more reliable than God
Deliverance comes only through political power
questions.correctAnswer: God is the true king and deliverer, and human kings may fail or be given in anger
questions.explanation: Verses 10-11 show God declaring Himself as king and questioning the ability of human judges and kings to save, while also noting kings were given in His anger and removed in wrath, guiding believers to trust God over human leaders.

questions.question: What does Hosea 13:7-8 suggest about God's character when dealing with sin?
options: God is both a watchful protector and a fierce judge
God is only patient and forgiving
questions.correctAnswer: God is both a watchful protector and a fierce judge
questions.explanation: Verses 7-8 portray God as a lion, leopard, and bear who observes and fiercely judges Israel for their rebellion, showing that God is watchful and just in dealing with sin.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 13:11 says that God was pleased when He gave Israel a king.
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:11 clearly states that God gave Israel a king in His anger and took him away in His wrath, indicating displeasure rather than pleasure.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 13:9 teaches that even though Israel has destroyed themselves, God remains their source of help.
questions.explanation: Verse 9 affirms that Israel has destroyed themselves, but in God is their help, encouraging trust in God despite personal failure.

questions.question: True or False: According to Hosea 13:12, Ephraim's sin is openly acknowledged and easily forgiven.
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:12 states that Ephraim's iniquity is bound up and his sin is hidden, meaning it is not openly acknowledged, which impedes forgiveness and repentance.

questions.question: How does Hosea 13:7-8 illustrate the consequences of forgetting God as described in Hosea 13:6?
options: Forgetting God leads to severe judgment likened to wild beasts attacking
Forgetting God causes immediate prosperity and peace
Forgetting God results in being protected by angels
Forgetting God has no real consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Forgetting God leads to severe judgment likened to wild beasts attacking
questions.explanation: Verse 6 shows Israel's heart was exalted and they forgot God, and verses 7-8 depict God responding as a fierce lion, leopard, and bear that will devour them, illustrating the serious consequences of forgetting God.

questions.question: What practical Christian living principle is taught by Hosea 13:9-10 regarding where to place one's trust?
options: Trust in God as the ultimate king and savior rather than human leaders
Trust primarily in human political systems
Trust in wealth and power for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in God as the ultimate king and savior rather than human leaders
questions.explanation: Verses 9-10 emphasize that despite Israel's failings, help and salvation come from God alone, not from kings or judges, encouraging believers to place trust in God above human authority.

hard.title: Hosea Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hosea Chapter 13.

questions.question: What does Hosea 13:13 describe coming upon Ephraim, illustrating his unwise nature?
options: The sorrows of a travailing woman
questions.correctAnswer: The sorrows of a travailing woman
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:13 states, 'The sorrows of a travailing woman shall come upon him: he is an unwise son; for he should not stay long in the place of the breaking forth of children,' highlighting the intense suffering and unwise position of Ephraim.

questions.question: According to Hosea 13:14, from what does the LORD promise to ransom and redeem Israel?
options: The power of the grave and death
questions.correctAnswer: The power of the grave and death
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:14 says, 'I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death,' showing God's promise to save Israel from death and the grave.

questions.question: What imagery is used in Hosea 13:15 to describe the coming judgment upon Ephraim?
options: An east wind from the wilderness drying up springs and fountains
A swarm of locusts devouring the crops
questions.correctAnswer: An east wind from the wilderness drying up springs and fountains
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:15 describes judgment with the metaphor of an east wind from the wilderness causing drought and spoiling treasures, indicating desolation.

questions.question: What fate does Hosea 13:16 pronounce upon Samaria due to its rebellion against God?
options: It shall become desolate, fall by the sword, and suffer cruel violence to infants and pregnant women
It shall be blessed with peace and prosperity
It shall be spared from destruction
It shall be taken captive but preserved
questions.correctAnswer: It shall become desolate, fall by the sword, and suffer cruel violence to infants and pregnant women
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:16 clearly states Samaria's desolation due to rebellion, including violent death of infants and women with child, emphasizing the severity of judgment.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God as the only savior, as stated in Hosea 13:4?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 43:11 states, 'I, even I, am the LORD; and beside me there is no saviour,' directly echoing Hosea 13:4's declaration of God's exclusive role as savior.

questions.question: What literary device is primarily used in Hosea 13:3 when describing the fate of Ephraim?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:3 uses similes comparing Ephraim to 'the morning cloud,' 'early dew,' 'chaff,' and 'smoke' to illustrate the fleeting and unstable nature of their existence.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'ransom' in Hosea 13:14 imply about God's action?
options: To release or redeem by payment
questions.correctAnswer: To release or redeem by payment
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'ransom' (padah) implies God’s redeeming action, releasing Israel from death’s power by paying a price, as stated in Hosea 13:14.

questions.question: In Hosea 13:11, what reason does God give for giving and then taking away a king from Israel?
options: Because of His anger and wrath
questions.correctAnswer: Because of His anger and wrath
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:11 says, 'I gave thee a king in mine anger, and took him away in my wrath,' indicating judgment rather than blessing.

questions.question: According to Hosea 13:9, where does Israel's help lie despite their self-destruction?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:9 clearly states, 'O Israel, thou hast destroyed thyself; but in me is thine help,' showing God as the true source of salvation.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of death's defeat mentioned in Hosea 13:14?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 15:54-55 speaks of death being swallowed up in victory, resonating with Hosea 13:14’s declaration of God’s destruction of death and the grave.

questions.question: What does Hosea 13:7 use to symbolize God's approach toward Israel due to their sins?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:7 states, 'I will be unto them as a lion: as a leopard by the way will I observe them,' symbolizing fierce judgment.

questions.question: According to Hosea 13:2, what have the people of Israel made according to their own understanding?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:2 states they made molten images of silver and idols according to their own understanding, reflecting idolatry.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 13:10 declares that God will be Israel's king and questions if any other can save them in their cities.
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:10 says, 'I will be thy king: where is any other that may save thee in all thy cities?' affirming God's kingship and exclusive power to save.

questions.question: True or False: Hosea 13:16 predicts that Samaria will be spared from destruction due to its allegiance to God.
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:16 predicts Samaria will become desolate and suffer violent destruction because of rebellion against God, not spared.

questions.question: What does Hosea 13:12 say about the nature of Ephraim's sin?
options: It is bound up and hidden
questions.correctAnswer: It is bound up and hidden
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:12 states, 'The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; his sin is hid,' indicating their sins are concealed but still present.

theological.title: Hosea Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hosea Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Hosea 13:1 indicate about Ephraim's initial state before sinning?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:1 states that 'When Ephraim spake trembling, he exalted himself in Israel,' indicating that Ephraim's fear led to pride before his downfall.

questions.question: According to Hosea 13:2, what did the people of Israel create as a form of idol worship?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:2 mentions that they 'have made them molten images of their silver,' reflecting their idolatry and turning away from God.

questions.question: What metaphor does Hosea use in 13:3 to describe the fleeting nature of Israel's faith?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:3 uses the metaphor 'as the morning cloud' to illustrate how quickly Israel's faith dissipates, like the early dew.

questions.question: What does Hosea 13:4 declare about the identity of the LORD?
questions.explanation: In Hosea 13:4, God declares, 'for there is no saviour beside me,' emphasizing His unique role as the one true God and savior.

questions.question: What condition does Hosea 13:6 describe regarding Israel's heart after being filled?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:6 states, 'therefore have they forgotten me,' indicating that their prosperity led to spiritual amnesia.

questions.question: What divine action does God describe in Hosea 13:8 towards unrepentant Israel?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:8 describes God as a bear that will rend their hearts, indicating His fierce judgment against their unfaithfulness.

questions.question: What does Hosea 13:9 imply about Israel's self-destruction?
options: It was a result of ignorance
It was due to external enemies
questions.correctAnswer: It was a result of ignorance
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:9 states, 'O Israel, thou hast destroyed thyself,' indicating that their downfall stemmed from their own actions and choices.

questions.question: What does Hosea 13:10 reveal about Israel's desire for leadership?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:10 reflects Israel's request for a king, showing their rejection of God's sovereign rule over them.

questions.question: What does Hosea 13:11 indicate about God's anger regarding Israel's king?
options: He gave them a king in anger
questions.correctAnswer: He gave them a king in anger
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:11 clearly states, 'I gave thee a king in mine anger,' indicating that their leadership was a judgment rather than a blessing.

questions.question: In Hosea 13:14, what does God promise regarding death and the grave?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:14 declares, 'I will ransom them from the power of the grave,' showcasing God's promise of salvation and redemption.

questions.question: What does Hosea 13:15 predict will happen to Ephraim due to God's judgment?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:15 indicates that 'his spring shall become dry,' symbolizing the impending judgment and loss of vitality due to their rebellion.

questions.question: What does Hosea 13:16 prophesy about Samaria's fate?
options: It will fall by the sword
questions.correctAnswer: It will fall by the sword
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:16 states, 'they shall fall by the sword,' indicating the severe consequences of Samaria's rebellion against God.

questions.question: What overarching theme can be drawn from Hosea 13:9 and 14 regarding Israel's reliance on God?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:9 shows Israel's self-destruction, while 13:14 indicates God's promise of redemption, highlighting their need for divine reliance.

questions.question: What does the combination of Hosea 13:4 and 13:14 reveal about God's nature?
options: He is distant from His people
He is both just and merciful
questions.correctAnswer: He is both just and merciful
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:4 emphasizes God's uniqueness as savior, while 13:14 reveals His mercy in ransoming His people, demonstrating His dual nature.

questions.question: What doctrine is illustrated by the promise in Hosea 13:14 concerning redemption?
questions.explanation: Hosea 13:14's promise of ransoming His people illustrates the doctrine of salvation by grace, emphasizing God's initiative in redemption.
